CLIMATE ACTION 
Climate Action Plan (CAP) 
• Meeting on utilising SEAI SEC funding for Energy Master Plan for Carrick-on-Shannon Climate Action 
SEC with ATU mentor (13 April 2026).  EMP to include - Energy Audit campaign, Case studies, Active 
Travel in the DZ study, Home Energy Upgrade campaign, EMP report and Final EMP Energy Upgrade 
Event.   
• Meeting of Energy WG on 15 April 2026.   
• IKC3 Programme has engaged 30 no participants (11 for the accredited pathway) in Co. Leitrim.    
The 3-month programme is designed to build capacity and partnerships for climate action through 
webinars and workshops and commenced on 14 April 2026. 
• Climate Action attended CARO networking event in Athlone on 15 April 2026 (Conference including 
guest speaker Mary Robinson) and 16 April 2026 (Field Trip, various case studies around Athlone 
area) 
• Department have committed to €50,000 funding for implementation of DZ actions, to be spent by 
mid-October.  Await final detail and eligibility criteria before mobilising actions. 
• Ongoing engagement with Community on bringing a climate course for over 55s to Co. Leitrim 
(with Jacinta Barrins) in September 
 
Biodiversity  
• Procurement documents prepared for issue to consultants to deliver projects under LBAF funding. 
(awaiting confirmation of funding from NPWS)  
• Engagement with PEACEPLUS team and community groups who have applied for PEACEPLUS 
biodiversity awareness grant.  
• Organisation of events and coordination with community groups to develop a programme of 
events for National Biodiversity Week in Co. Leitrim (15 – 24 May) 
• Participation in internal consultation workshop for ecology wetlands park in Carrick on Shannon

COMMUNITY AND INTERGATION 
Local Enhancement Programme 2026 
Leitrim’s allocation for 2026 is €119,043.40 for capital projects and purchases only. Initial review is 
complete and recommendations for the LCDC Assessment Committee have been prepared. 
 
Age Friendly Programme   
Discussions with AFI continue in relation to providing training to the OPC Chair and Vice-Chair. Theme is 
Communications Masterclass.  
 
Healthy Ireland 
Job advertisement for the new Healthy Ireland Coordinator closed with interviews currently taking 
place. 
Community Recognition Fund 
Leitrim has been allocated over €2.2 million under this funding programme, funding 16 capital 
projects throughout the county. All projects have commenced. As at the end of April 2026, 6 of these 
projects have been completed with funding fully drawn down from the Department of Rural and 
Community Development and an Gaeltacht.  
Love Where You Live 
The Love Where You Live Primary Schools Competition re now closed for entries and the Community 
Development and Climate Action Team of Leitrim County Council look forward to visiting all 
participation schools. The Love Where You Live 2026 Community Competition is now open for entries 
under comprise six categories, as follows: 
 
Green Community 
Green Estate 
Age Friendly Community 
Social Inclusion 
Community Achievement 
Gen Z Impact Award (new for 2026) 
 
Closing date for entries is 18th May 2026 
 
Playgrounds 
Leitrim County Council secured funding of €22,000 from the Department of Children, Disability and 
Equality an inclusive and accessible upgrade of Dristernan Playground, Drumshanbo.

Leitrim PEACEPLUS Action Plan (1.1) 
Local Community Regeneration & Transformation 
• Play & Art Therapy Centre, Drumkeeran - Works continuing onsite – building is roofed & sealed 
and on schedule for completion by Qtr3. 
• Construction works are due for completion mid-May followed by snagging. The official project 
title is Carrick-on-Shannon Youth Arts & Community Space, but it is intended to consult with the 
public on a name for the building. 
• Tender for MUGA in Ballinamore is currently being advertised on eTenders with a submission 
deadline of 3rd June 2026.  
 
Thriving & Peaceful Communities  
• QQI Level 7 – Participants attended face-to-face session in the W8 Manorhamilton & attended one 
online session during April.  
• Volunteer Support Programme – The Leitrim Volunteer Centre have been rolling out training in a 
number of locations as part of their programme. As well as community capacity training, first aid 
they are also delivering barista training which there has been keen interest in. 
• Virtual Reality Program Equipment – A quotation request was issued for the delivery of a series of 
workshop with young people using VR equipment. This will be delivered in a number of locations 
throughout the county. 
• Digital Camps for Young People – Harp Media are planning training camps for The Junction, 
Ballinamore, The Glens Centre and The Cornmill over the summer. Recruitment for these will be 
commencing in May 
 
Celebrating Cultural Diversity 
• Digital Camps for Young People – Harp Media are planning training camps for The Junction, 
Ballinamore, The Glens Centre and The Cornmill over the summer. Recruitment for these will be 
commencing in May. 
• An International Sports Day is being planned for the summer where coaches will deliver taster 
sessions in cricket, volleyball, badminton & table tennis. 
 
PEACEPLUS Shannonside Peace Arena (1.4) 
• The fourth Project Board meeting for 2026 took place in April, with attendance from SEUPB, the 
Department for Communities (NI), DRCDG and McAdam Design. 
• Procurement specialists ARVO commenced their review of the construction tender 
documentation in late April, with initial queries expected to be addressed in early May.  
• SEUPB requested a review of the Letter of Offer conditions to date; this is currently being 
progressed by LCC. 
• McAdam Design issued further updated external design imagery for the SRC site.                                                    
• LCC's Development Officer completed a review of the SRC website and social media channels and 
provided feedback to ensure compliance with the SEUPB - funded and approved 
communications plan.       
                                                               
Management 
• Crowleys DFK auditors have been working on certifying our claims. Under the Council Action Plan 
we have 10 Claims up on the Jems Portal from Oct 2023 to March 202. Claim periods are 
quarterly, claims 5 & 6 have been certified: 
Claim 5 - €31,442 
Claim 6 - €38,611

• Under the Shannonside Peace Arena there are 5 Claims on the portal from November 2024 to 
January 2025.  LCC have zero expenditure for first 2 claim periods. We have responded to detailed 
queries on Claim 4 and are awaiting certification on these.  
 
Local Community Safety Partnership 
The Community Safety Partnership meeting was held on 14th April 2026 in The Junction, Ballinamore. 
This facilitated session provided Partnership members with the opportunity to identify and discuss key 
community safety concerns and to prioritise emerging themes and ideas. Engagement on the day was 
strong and constructive, reflecting a high level of commitment across the Partnership. 
Feedback from the April session is currently being finalised and will inform the next stages of the 
Community Safety Plan. The public survey is at final draft stage and is expected to go live early next 
week. A communications plan is being developed to support the rollout, incorporating website content, 
traditional media, and social media messaging. 
In parallel, work is underway on two potential funding applications under the Community Safety Fund, 
which opened last week. These proposals are being developed in line with priorities emerging through 
consultation and partnership engagement 
Local Authority Integration Team (LAIT) 
The Integration Team delivered a total of ten clinics supporting individuals and families to access 
appropriate services. 
• 
Three clinics were held for Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection (BOTP). 
• 
Seven clinics were delivered across IPAS Centres. 
 
A total of two information sessions were delivered in April in collaboration with Library in Ballinamore 
and the Jesuit Refugee Society.  
 
The Wellbeing Advantage Workshop Series, a collaborative initiative between the Integration Team and 
Healthy Ireland, continued during April. The second workshop focused on Heart and Brain Health, 
followed by a third workshop on the Importance of Sleep and Nutrition. The programme includes a 
variety of wellbeing activities such as walking and running groups, alongside individual health 
assessments. 
 
An Art Workshop with young people from both IPAS centres in Leitrim commenced in April and was a 
collaborative project with Leitrim Volunteer Centre. The artwork created is inspired by the theme of 
‘Courage’, this year’s refugee week theme. The artwork will be showcased on Africa Day & during 
Refugee Week.

LIBRARY SERVICES 
 
 
Spring into Story time 
Many school classes attended ‘Spring into Storytime’ Events held across the branch network.  Some 
outreach Storytime sessions were also facilitated by staff. The ‘Spring into Storytime’ initiative is run 
across the county with fun and engaging story-times being delivered to young children as part of the 
national Right to Read Programme.  
Conversation on Books 
The Conversations on Books series continued in the The Dock on April 25th and featured the book ‘In Cold 
Blood’ by Truman Capote. This initiative is a collaboration between Leitrim Library Service and The 
Reading Room Bookshop in Carrick-on-Shannon. The event, held at The Dock was very well attended. 
The programme continues to draw readers from across the county and further afield. 
Dementia Inclusive Club 
The Dementia Inclusive Social Club continues in Carrick on-Shannon and Mohill Library. The club is a 
social gathering where people can access information and support, meet other people and exchange 
ideas and experiences.

ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT 
STEM Passport for Inclusion- Maynooth University & ATU 
Schools continue their assignments to ATU.  Date of November 2nd confirmed for Graduation of Leitrim 
Students. The STEM Passport for Inclusion industry event takes place in June.  
 
Dream Space Showcase 
Two Leitrim groups are participating in the national Microsoft Dream Space event taking place in May in 
Microsoft’s Headquarters.  
 
Carrick on Shannon Community CCTV Scheme Extension 
Consultants met with Electric Skyline in terms of re-costing the phase 2 a first report was received in 
April with revisions required.  
 
Carrick on Shannon Business Campus (Enterprise Hub) 
Meetings with BABLE GmbH and the working group continued in relation to the priming phase of the 
proposed Enterprise Hub at the Carrick-on-Shannon Business Campus. Stakeholder consultations took 
place during March, and further meetings are planned during April. 
 
Leitrim Economic Forum  
The most recent meeting of the Economic Forum took place on May 8th, 2026.  Work continues on the 
Development of the Economic and Skills strategy for Leitrim and on the planning of the Leitrim 
Ambassadors Summit, two initiatives of the Forum.  The summit is scheduled for September 2026. 
 
Shaping Leitrim- A Place led Economic and Skills Strategy for Leitrim 2026-2035 
Bi-weekly meetings are taking place with BABLE Smart cities as the consultation phase for the new 
strategy continues. One to one stakeholder meetings continued in April. The consultation survey closed 
in April, and the preliminary results were presented to the Economic Forum meeting. Workshops will be 
scheduled for May.  
 
Global Business Network 
The next meeting of the group is scheduled for 12th May 2026. 
 
Remote Working Marketing Campaign 
Planning meetings continued during April, to finalise case study participants and campaign 
ambassadors for the social media video content for the campaign.  Ambassadors include Norah Casey, 
Dave Duke and Bryan Dobson. The campaign title “Most Definitely Leitrim” has been selected.  
 
DRCDG Funded Schemes 
A Clár webinar was hosted during April, outlining the changes to the 2026 scheme. 
The scheme is open for Expressions of Interest until 14th May.  
The Building and Land Acquisition Measure opened again during April and remains open for Expressions 
of Interest until 15th May.

TOURISM 
Marketing  
As part of the ongoing Destination Leitrim marketing campaign, the county received excellent national 
exposure through a series of high impact media partnerships: 
• 
Ireland AM - featured a Leitrim prize giveaway sponsored by Lough Rynn Castle Estate & Gardens, 
showcasing the county’s luxury hospitality offering. 
• 
Lyric FM - highlighted the charm and character of Leitrim Village, reinforcing its appeal as a 
peaceful getaway with a giveaway at Leitrim Quay Self Catering Cottages.  
• 
RTÉ 2FM – Tracey Clifford Show promoted Drumhierney Woodland Hideaway, spotlighting 
Leitrim’s unique nature-based accommodation experiences. 
 
These collaborations significantly boosted national awareness and strengthened Leitrim’s position as a 
desirable short break destination, driving both interest and intent among domestic travelers. 
 
Influencer Marketing 
A successful influencer activation took place when Timmy Mallett cycled through the county, staying in 
Maguires Cottages Drumshanbo, visiting The Landmark Hotel, and exploring Lough Rynn. 
 
Social Media 
We continue to maintain a strong presence across all major social media platforms. 
The Winter Winner of our photography competition has been selected and will be featured in the End of 
Year Leitrim Calendar. 
 
PR  
Preparation is underway for a countywide PR campaign focused on positive tourism stories. The goal is 
to secure strong national and international media coverage throughout the year, highlighting Leitrim’s 
unique experiences, people, and landscapes. 
 
Tourism Trade Event – Destination Reconnect Leitrim 
The event, hosted at Drumhierney Woodland Hideaway and facilitated by John Grahams, delivered an 
exceptionally collaborative and energising gathering for the local tourism sector. The event saw a strong 
turnout, with businesses actively engaging, sharing insights, and contributing to a collective vision for 
the county’s tourism future. 
 
Collaboration was the central theme of the day, and this focus shaped both the discussions and the 
outcomes. Key insights included: 
• 
Shared motivation rooted in community, authenticity, and a unified sense of purpose across the 
sector. 
• 
Cross sector collaboration identified as a major opportunity, with participants expressing a clear 
appetite for working more closely together. 
• 
Improved communication highlighted as essential to unlocking stronger partnerships and 
reducing barriers. 
• 
Targeted training recognised as a key enabler to support business growth and enhance visitor 
experiences. 
 
The event reinforced a powerful message, ‘Leitrim’s tourism success is strongest when built together with 
collaboration at the heart of every step forward’.

LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE (LEO) 
Training, Mentoring & Export      
A number of people received training in April as we ran a series of courses such as A Layman's Guide to 
Income Tax & Revenue Online Services, Cap Cut Training, Creative Connections workshop, How to 
Develop a Winning Business Plan and a Marketing Advice Clinic. Assistance is also available on Export 
related issues and can be booked online free of charge to discuss any issues facing businesses or 
identifying and managing opportunities available for exporting.  
 
All In A Days Work Programmes & Associated Financial Supports 
The “All In A Days Work” campaign continues to be rolled out on the areas of Lean, Green and Digital 
supports.  There is significant growth in demand for all three supports, in particular the Energy Efficiency 
Grant (EEG) and Grow Digital (GD) Voucher.   The EEG, with up to 75% of eligible costs up to a maximum 
grant of €10,000 can be supported following the completion of a Green for Business, Green Start or a 
SEAI Energy Audit.   The GD voucher is a grant covering 50% of eligible costs (minimum grant of €500 up 
to a maximum grant of €5,000) limited to new software subscriptions for a period of 12 and training and 
configuration of the software. 
 
Atlantic Economic Corridor Update:  
Interreg Europe Digital Rural: Leitrim continues its partnership under Interreg Europe. The Digital Rural 
Project empowers rural communities through smart technologies and collaborative policymaking to 
foster sustainable regional development.  
 
PEACE Plus – DS3 Project 
Workshops and clinics with the Mobile Fab Lab are ongoing under the DS3 Project under PEACE Plus 
(Smart Towns & Villages). The project will run until July 2028 and offers free digital mentoring, skills 
development and community-focused digital inclusion activities. This programme is offered to SMEs, 
micro businesses, community/voluntary groups and individuals located in rural towns and villages. 
Schools can also avail of workshops with the mobile labs. 
 
Creative Heartlands 
The programme ‘Creative Heartlands on Screen’ continues with training and mentoring for the screen 
sector in Leitrim, Sligo and Roscommon with funding from Screen Ireland. A comprehensive mentorship 
programme has been established. Partnership with Creative Skillsnet continues and is entering its third 
year.  
 
Northwest Regional Enterprise Plan Implementation 
Northwest Vision Development 
The 3 Chief Executives from Leitrim/Sligo/Donegal are collaborating to develop a Northwest Region 
Vision which will feed into the REP development in 2026. Leitrim CoCo is represented on the project by 
Director of Economic Development and the NW REP Programme Manager.  The draft document was 
considered by the group and further feedback given to the consultants.  A revised document is expected 
in April.   
 
Energy working group 
A multi-agency supported project is underway which will explore the opportunities available to both the 
North West and West Regions with available unused energy from our renewable energy sources e.g. 
onshore wind energy. Opportunities being explored are green energy parks, marketing, hydrogen etc. 
Leitrim CoCo is represented on the project by Director of Economic Development and the NW REP 
Programme Manager. A presentation on the report was made to the CEs and Directors of Economic

12 
 
Development across the four sponsoring counties, Donegal, Leitrim, Sligo and Mayo on 25th March by 
consultants on the project, GDG Consulting.  A presentation of the report is hoped to be made to the 
steering committee in April where next steps on hosting regional/online seminars will be discussed.  
 
10xNW 2026 
The North West Region came together to host the 10xNW entrepreneurship exchange in February 2026 in 
Leitrim. After a very successful event the11 entrepreneurs and mentors continue to engage with each 
other throughout March as part of the commitment under the programme.  
 
Next REP development 
The Final report of the Northwest Regional Enterprise Plan 2022-2025 is currently in draft form and was 
submitted to DETE in mid-January.  Once approved by DETE will be published on DETE website.  
Currently DETE are undergoing a review of the REP’s with the intention of taking recommendations from 
the review towards the next REP development which is due to kick off Q2 2026. 
 
TOWN REGENERATION 
In April 2026, 3 new Funding schemes for refurbishment of Vacant properties. 
  
Vacant Above the Shop Grant 
Tackling vacancy and dereliction is a key priority under the national housing plan Delivering Homes, 
Building Communities 2025-2030, with existing grants and schemes supporting bringing vacant and 
derelict properties back into use being improved and expanded. Their use will ensure that additional 
homes are provided by refurbishing existing properties and repurposing ‘above the shop’ and vacant 
commercial space.2. VPRG Scheme Outline (including conversion of commercial / public use building) 
 
VPRG, Conversion of former Commercial/ Public Use Building 
Tackling vacancy and dereliction is a key priority under the national housing plan Delivering Homes, 
Building Communities 2025-2030, with existing grants and schemes supporting bringing vacant and 
derelict properties back into use being improved and expanded. 
 
Expert Advice Grant-Vacant Homes 
Expert Advice Grant for Vacant Above the Shop Conversions and Conversion of former commercial / public 
use buildings to residential units. The Expert Advice Grant provides funding of up to €5,000 (the total grant 
sought cannot exceed 67% of the overall cost inclusive of VAT). 
 
Croí Conaithe – Vacant Property Refurbishment Grants 
March & April 2026 – 25 new applications were received, total number of applications in 2026 is 44. During 
this reporting period, 9 grant payments were processed 2026. 
 
Town Team Meeting 
There was 1 town meeting that occurred in April, Dromahair Town Team, which was attended by Leitrim 
County Council staff on the 14th of April. 
 
Dromahair 
Dromahair Town Team held a very successful public town team meeting to give the people of Dromahair 
a better perspective on their function and to give an update on their work so far. They also be put out an 
expression of interest for anyone who would like to join their wider town team and asked for the people 
of Dromahair to give the ideas and feedback on possible projects going forward.

The Energy Efficiency Retrofit Scheme is ongoing with the focus on targeting the houses with the lowest

Forward Planning 
Variation to County Development Plan 2023-2029 
The proposed draft Variation to the County Development Plan 2023-2029 was published on 15th April 
with submissions invited by 13th May 2026.    
Residential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) 
Draft RZLT maps were published on Friday 30th January and public consultation will run until April 1st. 2 
no. submissions were received requesting lands to be dezoned, one of which relates to a site proposed 
to be rezoned from residential use to agriculture in the variation. All of the information relating to the 
RZLT is on our website.
